Quinolinic Acid is directly linked to Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which in turn is targeted by n-acetyl serotonin. This chain of interactions implies that Quinolinic Acid may influence the activity of n-acetyl serotonin, potentially modulating the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The presence of a direct target relationship between Quinolinic Acid and the transporter suggests a possible role in anion transport regulation, possibly through the modulation of serotonin signaling. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Quinolinic Acid could affect transporter activity, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
